Team —

Ahead of the QBR next week I pulled together a short set of capacity scenarios and a first-pass unit-econ model for GPU spend under each. Attached: capacity-scenarios-v2.xlsx (tabbed by 'conservative / target / aggressive') and batching-cache-run-summary.pdf (sample runs from our staging load). Goal for this thread: lock a recommendations slide and a single ask for execs (SLA vs. cost tradeoff) by EOD Wednesday so the GTM leads can bake in messaging.

Key asks:
- Vivek: sanity-check utilization targets (we used 42%, 58%, 72%) and confirm whether reserved vs spot mixes assumed are realistic for Dedicated.
- Monica: add the latency tail impact for the aggressive batching profile and confirm if KV/prefix cache coverage assumptions are reasonable.
- Neha: confirm any compliance/regulatory constraints that would make private deployments materially more expensive in EU.
- Aditya: confirm which demos/customers to highlight as pressure points in the QBR (we have Orion Analytics and one large retailer flagged).

Notes:
- The scenarios model per-token GPU cost at multiple quantization levels; the aggressive scenario assumes 4-bit quantization on t2 variants and 95% cache hit in prefix cache.
- We should explicitly call out the fall-back policy if capacity is constrained (route-to-smaller-model + degraded throughput).

Attachments referenced: capacity-scenarios-v2.xlsx (master workbook), batching-cache-run-summary.pdf (latency percentiles), okr-alignment-notes.docx (working notes).

I'll consolidate by Wednesday 18:00 PT. Please reply in-thread with short numeric confirmations — we need things in the deck.

Thanks,
Rachel

Rachel — thanks for pulling this together. Quick read-through and notes below.

Summary answers:
- Utilization targets: the 42/58/72% bands look fine as long as we explicitly call out expected p50 vs p95 latency in each. For Dedicated, assume reserved:spot = 80:20 for conservative, 60:40 target, 40:60 aggressive (that changes unit-cost by ~9% in the workbook).
- Quant and cache assumptions: 4-bit on t2 is plausible for many of our smaller models; for L4-family large-chat models I'd call it risky without additional evals. If we gate quantization by model family the aggressive curve should be annotated as "partial quantization".
- Batch/caching impact: we saw ~22% token-cost reduction in the last batching experiment when KV prefix hit rate >88% but p95 latency climbed ~120ms for interactive workloads.

Edits I made to the workbook (see attached): added a 'reserve/spot mix' slider and a model-family toggle to separate safety checks for quant. Also added a sensitivity tab showing unit-cost delta if cache hit drops 10 points.

Operational ask: we need a single fallback-scenario statement for the deck. Proposal: "If aggregate utilization exceeds 75% for > 12 hours, automatically shift non-critical traffic to lower-cost model variants and trigger a scale-up request to ops with 30-min SLA." Thoughts?

–Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime

Adding a couple of quick items from the ops experiments — pasted highlights and a Drive link to the latency plots (public within company):

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1fK_capacity-scenarios

Highlights:
- Aggressive batching (batch size tuned to 3-6 tokens/req) reduced cost-per-token by ~28% in long tail, but for interactive flows p95 latency increased 100–180ms depending on shard placement.
- KV prefix cache: moving from 70% -> 90% hit reduces GPU token cost by ~18% but requires ~2.5x memory footprint for KV store; plan tradeoff vs dedicated node counts.
- Suggest we include a 'user-impact' row in the QBR slide: expected latency delta for high-frequency interactive customers (this helps GTM pick examples).

Also, I've attached a short csv in the Drive with the run parameters and a small chart in the deck. Will keep refining.
